core.prompt:
Create a coherent set of SIX separate MOBILE portrait screen designs for AISLEY Rider V2, the existing native Flutter Android courier app. Design references only. Every screen should be a separate named screen resource, not a montage or website. 390x844 logical portrait, scroll when needed.
Authority: preserve existing Material 3 controls and labels. Neutral #F7F7F8 canvas, white surfaces, ink #202024, secondary #55555D, border #E2E2E6, magenta primary #C00065. Roboto Flex stands in for platform Material font; 24px titles, 16px body, readable 14px metadata, 48px targets, 16px margins, 10px buttons and 12px flat cards. No gradients, lavender canvas, hero banners, decorative photography, slide gestures, floating pill nav or oversized identity cards. Magenta limited to next action/selection. Plain list rows and compact task context.
ROOTS have exactly Home / Work / Task messages / Account bottom NavigationBar with full visible labels. PUSHED screens have Back and no bottom nav. Synthetic demonstration data only: Mika Santos, Example Logistics, Main hub, ORD-DEMO-1042/1043, Pasig/Marikina. No real PII, secrets, evidence, readable QR/barcodes, raw paths, backend jargon, internal IDs, invented eligibility facts or certification.
1. V2 Home (root selected Home): AISLEY Rider app bar and Notifications bell; compact name and read-only organization/hub; Pickup orders and Delivery work shortcuts; Active work section one final-mile accepted reference ORD-DEMO-1042/Pasig with View task; Available work one first-mile offer ORD-DEMO-1043/Marikina Review task. Each section Last refreshed 09:41, View all, no totals. One calm inline refresh-failed state retains prior available row labelled Stale and Retry. Home taps only navigate. No online toggle, earnings, GPS, ETA or mutation.
2. V2 Work (root selected Work): title Work. Exactly five familiar ListTile rows: Pickup orders — Seller pickups and hub handoff; Delivery work — Photo proof and delivery review; Final-mile batches — Review individual parcel decisions; Linehaul jobs — Assigned hub transfers and company-truck routes; Delivery history — Completed deliveries. No stats/counters, help icons, authority banners or dispatch controls.
3. V2 Task details (pushed offered final-mile): reference ORD-DEMO-1042, Final mile, Delivery offered. Origin Example Logistics · Main hub, destination area Pasig City, one parcel. Primary Accept delivery, secondary Reject offer (reason step) and Message Logistics. No Buyer contact/full address before acceptance, no route action for offers, no bulk accept, no cash promise, no invented handling/zone/weight.
4. V2 Pickup scan review (pushed accepted first-mile): reference ORD-DEMO-1043, First mile, Pickup accepted, Example shop · Marikina City. Read-only captured tracking identifier DEMO-1043 with clear label Scanned code. Automatically detected Code 128, Scan again secondary. Primary Confirm pickup. Capture alone never confirms custody. NO editable identifier, manual input, type selector, fake barcode decoration or final-mile transfer claim.
5. V2 Delivery photo and cash (pushed accepted final-mile): ORD-DEMO-1042, Delivery accepted, authorized synthetic destination area Pasig City. Selected photo represented by neutral local-preview panel, no actual personal photo, secondary Retake/Choose photo/Remove. Cash to collect PHP 115.00, unchecked checkbox 'I collected PHP 115.00'. Exact primary label Delivered, visibly disabled until cash acknowledgment and photo prerequisites hold. Next submission goes to Logistics review, never instant delivered/paid. No mandatory transit timeline, signature, recipient OTP, sliders, GPS or pay amounts entry.
6. V2 Task messages (root selected Task messages): title Task messages; two compact task-linked conversation rows with safe Logistics/Seller labels, visible task reference/leg, short plain-text demo previews, text unread indication; read-only thread state where appropriate. Refresh recovery inline. No global people directory/new-chat FAB, broadcast, support mixing or presence claims.
Return each as a separate screen with retrieval IDs and screenshot.

auxiliary.prompt:
# AISLEY Rider V2 — reference-only Flutter Material 3
Repository docs/design-courier.md is authoritative. A courier acts on one parcel/task leg at a time within a server-derived organization and sole hub. Existing root tabs: Home, Work, Task messages, Account. Pushed routes use Back without bottom navigation. Familiar Material NavigationBar selection indicator, ordinary tap buttons, one dominant next action. 48px targets, scrollable content, 16px margins, 10px controls, 12px cards. Titles 24px, body 16px, metadata 14px. Neutral light #F7F7F8 / #FFFFFF / ink #202024 / secondary #55555D / border #E2E2E6, primary #C00065. Dark #141416 / #1C1C1E / ink #F3F3F5 / secondary #C6C6CE / primary #FF85BD.
No slide actions, earnings, payout/performance, shift/availability toggle, live GPS, typing/presence, arbitrary fleet controls, bulk acceptance, global people directory, chat system alerts, biometrics, app PIN, recipient signatures/OTP, incident/SOS or unimplemented capabilities. No hero, gradients, glass, ornamental photos, decorative barcodes, technical banners or fake certifications. Do not invent metadata to fill space.
Home has bounded read-only sections and per-section freshness/failure, never queue totals. Work contains Pickup orders, Delivery work, Final-mile batches, Linehaul jobs, Delivery history. Account contains Profile, Security, Vehicle and documents, Appearance, Policies, Support tickets, Sign out.
First-mile pickup is scan-only QR/Code128 candidate capture + review + explicit Confirm pickup; no manual/type entry. Final-mile offers have per-parcel accept/reject; hub handoff is task-bound without identifier. Direct accepted final-mile delivery: photo + exact COD acknowledgment + Delivered intent; server/Logistics confirms delivered. Never claim custody/payment from a tap.
Registration details/evidence/review first, dedicated OTP next, successful verification automatically submits once. No account/session until registration persistence; Courier waits for Logistics approval. No password recovery UI. Combined Terms/Privacy consent has two unchecked version-bound checkboxes, one Accept.
Designs are synthetic static references; tool-generated descriptions do not establish implemented behavior or accessibility compliance.
Generate TEN additional distinct named mobile portrait screen resources for the existing AISLEY Rider V2 app. Each independently retrievable screen, not a montage. designSystemCorrection.requestedMarkdown:
# AISLEY Rider V2 — reference-only Flutter Material 3
Repository docs/design-courier.md is authoritative. A courier acts on one parcel/task leg at a time within a server-derived organization and sole hub. Existing root tabs: Home, Work, Task messages, Account. Pushed routes use Back without bottom navigation. Familiar Material NavigationBar selection indicator, ordinary tap buttons, one dominant next action. 48px targets, scrollable content, 16px margins, 10px controls, 12px cards. Titles 24px, body 16px, metadata 14px. Neutral light #F7F7F8 / #FFFFFF / ink #202024 / secondary #55555D / border #E2E2E6, primary #C00065. Dark #141416 / #1C1C1E / ink #F3F3F5 / secondary #C6C6CE / primary #FF85BD.
No slide actions, earnings, payout/performance, shift/availability toggle, live GPS, typing/presence, arbitrary fleet controls, bulk acceptance, global people directory, chat system alerts, biometrics, app PIN, recipient signatures/OTP, incident/SOS or unimplemented capabilities. No hero, gradients, glass, ornamental photos, decorative barcodes, technical banners or fake certifications. Do not invent metadata to fill space.
Home has bounded read-only sections and per-section freshness/failure, never queue totals. Work contains Pickup orders, Delivery work, Final-mile batches, Linehaul jobs, Delivery history. Account contains Profile, Security, Vehicle and documents, Appearance, Policies, Support tickets, Sign out.
First-mile pickup is scan-only QR/Code128 candidate capture + review + explicit Confirm pickup; no manual/type entry. Final-mile offers have per-parcel accept/reject; hub handoff is task-bound without identifier. Direct accepted final-mile delivery: photo + exact COD acknowledgment + Delivered intent; server/Logistics confirms delivered. Never claim custody/payment from a tap.
Registration details/evidence/review first, dedicated OTP next, successful verification automatically submits once. No account/session until registration persistence; Courier waits for Logistics approval. No password recovery UI. Combined Terms/Privacy consent has two unchecked version-bound checkboxes, one Accept.
Designs are synthetic static references; tool-generated descriptions do not establish implemented behavior or accessibility compliance.

I have refined all 16 AISLEY Rider mobile screens to strict Flutter Material 3 standards, removing all invented operations data, technical badges, and unsupported claims while establishing consistent visual craft.

1. **Global Material 3 & Design Consistency:**
   - **Typography:** Strictly enforced sans-serif (Roboto Flex) across every screen (correcting the serif typography in Work). Unified hierarchy to Title 24px, Body 16px, and Metadata 14px.
   - **Color & Surfaces:** Clean `#F7F7F8` background, crisp white container cards, `#202024` primary ink, `#55555D` secondary text, and single brand primary `#C00065`.
   - **Clean Components:** Stripped away all non-standard left-edge accent stripes, square icon wrappers, decorative version badges, and pseudo-metric counters.
   - **Navigation:** Standardized root bottom navigation across main views with exact case (`Home`, `Work`, `Task messages`, `Account`) and standard Material NavigationBar pill indicator.

2. **Per-Screen Highlights:**
   - **Home (`V3 Home`):** Removed rider ID 8842 and top-bar hamburger; identity card is now compact; replaced icon-top shortcut cards with standard labeled actions; cleaned active and cached lists.
   - **Work (`V3 Work`):** Switched to clean sans-serif typography; removed menu/bell; 5 plain rows with chevrons; full `Task messages` bottom navigation label.
